did_you_know.text: Did you know? The psalm opens with the heading “A Song of Ascents” and invites all the servants of the LORD to bless him.
Did you know? Verse 1 says that the servants of the LORD stand in the house of the LORD “by night,” emphasizing worship of the LORD even during the nighttime hours.
Did you know? The phrase “all the servants of the LORD” addresses everyone who serves the LORD, not just one individual.
Did you know? Verse 2 contains two brief commands: lift your hands toward the sanctuary and bless the LORD.
Did you know? The lifting of the hands is described in the verse as a symbol of turning toward the sanctuary as part of blessing the LORD.
Did you know? After the call for the servants of the LORD to bless him, a reciprocal blessing appears: “May the LORD bless you from Zion.”
Did you know? The final verse presents the LORD as the one “who made heaven and earth,” that is, the Creator of heaven and earth.
Did you know? The psalm creates a structure of mutual blessing: the servants of the LORD bless him, and the LORD blesses them from Zion.
